This application coming on for Admission this day, the court
 passed the following:
 Order

This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR registered at Crime No.271/2022 for the offence punishable under Sections 376 of IPC and Sections 3(2)(v) and 3(1)
(w)(i) of SC/ST Act.

As per prosecution story, the prosecutrix has lodged a written complaint on 29/04/22 at Police Station Gola ka Mandir, Gwalior against the petitioner-accused alleging that she had been living with her children in Birla Nagar Gwalior from almost four years back as she was not treated well by Kuldeep Singh Tomar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115387770/
1 her husband.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She got acquainted with the petitioner in the year 2020.
The petitioner-accused proposed her for marriage.
When she informed that she had already married, the petitioner-accused said that he had no objection on her being married.
Upon the promise of marriage by petitioner-accused, she engaged in sexual relationship with him.
The prosecutrix and the accused made physical relations on many occasions and last time on 22/04/22 they had sex in the house of prosecutrix.

However, on 28/04/22 the petitioner-accused told the prosecutrix that he had been getting many good marriage proposals and that he would marry with some other woman and was not interested in marrying the prosecutrix.
Thereafter she filed complaint upon which this FIR is registered U/s 376 of IPC and Sections 3(2)(v) and 3(1)(w)(i) of SC/ST Act.

Learned counsel for petitioner argued that the present FIR and consequential proceedings are sheer abuse of process of law as the prosecutrix is a married woman and therefore, question of promise of marriage does not arise.
Her marriage was not severed by a decree of divorce.
Since the marriage of the prosecutrix is still in subsistence second marriage can not be performed.
The physical relation between the prosecutrix and the petitioner is consensual in nature, therefore, the ingredients of offence of Section 376 of IPC do not attract.
Thus this petition be allowed and the FIR and consequential proceedings be quashed.

On the other hand, the petition is vehemently opposed by the counsel for the respondents and it has been submitted that from the FIR, it is primafacie appears that the petitioner on the false pretext of marriage has succeeded in developing relationship with prosecutrix and committed rape upon her.
Therefore, the petition be dismissed.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
From plain reading of the FIR lodged by the prosecutrix it is apparent that she is a married woman having two children.
Annexure P-1 is the complaint dated 12.04.2022 jointly filed by the prosecutix and the petitioner-accused before the police authority seeking protection against her own husband.

The prosecutix and the petitioner-accused have also filed a writ petition bearing W.P. No. 9107 of 2022 before this Court seeking protection against the husband of prosecutrix stating therein that she (the prosecutrix) and the petitioner were living in live-in relationship for last one year.
The prosecutrix prayed that her husband is causing obstacles in her relationship with the petitioner and threatening her to kill.
Therefore, protection be granted to them.
The record also reveals that the prosecutrix and her husband are still married as no decree of divorce is not granted.
In view of the above when the prosecutrix is already married, the promise alleged to have been made by the accused to marry her is a promise which is not enforceable in law.
Such an unenforceable and illegal promise cannot be a basis for the prosecution under Section 376 of IPC and therefore no question of any false promise to marry arises.

Since the prosecutrix is a married woman and she knew that legal marriage with the petitioner was not possible under the law, therefore, it can not be said that her engaging in sexual relationship with the petitioner was under the pretext of promise of marriage.

The fact that prosecutrix filed a writ petition before this Court for protection of the petitioner and herself against her legally wedded husband stating therein that she and present petitioner are living Kuldeep Singh Tomar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115387770/
2 in live-in relationship for almost one year, shows that the physical relationship between prosecutrix and the petitioner were consensual in nature and therefore, ingredients of Section 376 of IPC do not attract.
